title: A progress note, not a report
intro: A checkpoint is what the next worker would need if you stopped now. It is capped in length on purpose: past the cap you are writing a handover, and it says so.

scenarios.title: Recording progress
scenarios.explain: The file is written atomically at mode 0600 and is never staged. Its name carries the timestamp, branch and head, so a record can be placed without opening it.

scenarios.title: With no active task
scenarios.explain: A checkpoint belongs to the episode, not to a task. The record is written and its `task_id` is `none`, which is a fact a later reader can place; the ledger event it emits carries no `task_id` at all, because every reader of that event collects the field's distinct values as task identifiers. This scenario expected exit 12 until ADR 0041: refusing here meant that finishing a task silenced progress records for every episode after it, which is exactly what happened to this repository for six days from 2026-09-05.
